title: Common commands and their equivalents across the three systems

videos.script: How much space is left on the disk? Which program is using the processor? Where is the file with the client's name in it? Ana asks these questions every week, on three systems, and each system spells the answer differently. {{questions}} The good news is that the questions are always the same handful. About the machine, its processes, its disks, its files and its settings. Learn the handful once, and the three vocabularies become a table you can keep in your head. {{handful}} Linux and macOS share most of theirs, because both come from Unix. Windows has two, the Command Prompt's short old words and PowerShell's long descriptive ones. And PowerShell, alone among them, runs on all three systems. {{families}} In this lesson you will ask each question on Linux and in PowerShell, on the same machine. You will see the Command Prompt and macOS versions beside them, and finish with one table that answers all of them at once. {{steps}} The transcripts come from lesson 3's server, in bash and in PowerShell 7. The Windows and macOS commands are shown, not run. {{honest}}
